Zhang atlas figures: visual grammar and styles

Source: vignettes/atlas-figure-styles.Rmd
atlas-figure-styles.Rmd

Scope and source verification

The API provides 23 structural styles across matrices, distributions, effect estimates, set intersections and networks, alongside three reusable atlas themes. Structural styles change panel geometry: triangles, rings, annotation tracks, paired trajectories, split densities, forests, UpSet, clone trees and weighted chord ribbons. Typography remains 8 pt. They do not reproduce the papers’ biological results or guarantee identical colors, coordinates, clustering or panel layout. style = "classic" retains each function’s original defaults. Explicit palettes and existing embedding (nebula, glass) and Sankey (A, B, C) styles remain available.

The six papers below are the source set. Main figures were inspected for NK, B, myeloid, fibroblast and CM. For the Science T-cell paper, figure-caption descriptions were accessible, but the figure images were not independently inspected; its entries are provisional layout classifications. Supplementary and extended-data figures are not an exhaustive part of this inventory. The fibroblast paper is a cross-tissue atlas with cancer analyses. The Nature paper defines cellular modules, which are different from gene modules.

papers <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "zhang-atlas-papers.csv",
                              package = "Shennong"))
papers$Article <- sprintf("[%s (%s), %s](https://doi.org/%s)",
  papers$authors, papers$year, papers$journal, papers$doi)
knitr::kable(papers[c("paper", "title", "Article", "verification")])
paper title Article verification
NK A pan-cancer single-cell panorama of human natural killer cells Tang et al. (2023), Cell figures_and_captions
T Pan-cancer single-cell landscape of tumor-infiltrating T cells Zheng et al. (2021), Science captions_only
B Pan-cancer single-cell dissection reveals phenotypically distinct B cell subtypes Yang et al. (2024), Cell figures_and_captions
Myeloid A pan-cancer single-cell transcriptional atlas of tumor infiltrating myeloid cells Cheng et al. (2021), Cell figures_and_captions
Fibroblast Cross-tissue human fibroblast atlas reveals myofibroblast subtypes with distinct roles in immune modulation Gao et al. (2024), Cancer Cell figures_and_captions
CM Cross-tissue multicellular coordination and its rewiring in cancer Shi et al. (2025), Nature figures_and_captions_plus_Fig2c_source_data

Choose a geometry before choosing a style

Visual family Representative panels Input meaning and Shennong route
Embedding and feature maps NK 1C–D, 3C–D; B 5D–G sn_plot_dim(), sn_plot_feature() preserve supplied embedding coordinates; no velocity or new embedding is inferred.
Marker dots Myeloid 1E; NK 3E; B 5F; fibroblast 3A sn_plot_dot(style = "atlas_outline"): color is expression, size is percent expressing. Named feature lists form marker blocks.
Independent bubble encodings Fibroblast 1F; NK 6B–C; T 2A sn_plot_matrix(type = "bubble", size = ...): supply Ro/e, interaction potential or effect as color, and frequency, significance or effect as area. Legend titles must name the actual quantities.
Expression heatmaps NK 3A–B; B 5I; myeloid 3B sn_plot_heatmap() keeps the chosen cell/average mode and assay/layer. Paper styles use the ggplot renderer.
Quantitative matrices B 4A; CM 2c, 5f; fibroblast 5A sn_plot_matrix() preserves supplied Ro/e, correlation, activity or model coefficients, including NA. Optional blocks and clustering are explicit.
Summary bars T 1D–E sn_plot_barplot(stat = "summary", errorbar = "sd", style = "atlas") preserves sample means and SD; select SD versus SE explicitly.
Sample composition NK 2B–D; myeloid 3E; B 2A sn_plot_sample_boxplot() and sn_plot_sample_bar() retain sample denominators. Samples, not cells, are biological replicates.
Distributions NK 3G; B 5H; CM 4e sn_plot_distribution(), sn_plot_violin(): distinguish cell-level distributions from sample-aggregated values with sample_by.
Correlations and fitted trends NK 6I; B 2B; myeloid 7E sn_plot_association() retains the chosen correlation and fit. Style does not change test units or P values.
Differential expression and enrichment NK 4; fibroblast 2E–G, 4A–B sn_plot_de(), sn_plot_enrichment() style existing statistics; significance thresholds remain analysis choices.
Survival and effect intervals NK 5D–E; fibroblast 4G–H; T 5B sn_plot_survival() renders an existing survival result. A linear coefficient forest (T 4B) must not be interpreted as a Cox HR forest.
Communication and module networks NK 6; CM 2b, 5i; fibroblast 3I sn_plot_communication() styles its native score; sn_plot_network() renders supplied edges and nodes. The latter also accepts fixed coordinates for matched network comparisons.
Spatial coordinates and features Fibroblast 5D–F; CM 3, 4g sn_plot_spatial*() uses existing coordinates/sections. Histology and segmented-cell outlines require their original image assets.
Set, tree and circular layouts B 2C/3D/4L; CM 4c; fibroblast 6B sn_plot_overlap(style="upset"), sn_plot_network(style="clone_tree"/"chord"), sn_plot_matrix(style="split_triangle"/"circular"). Supply sets, topology and scores explicitly.

Circular phylogenetic dendrograms, Venn diagrams, FACS gates, ATAC tracks, microscopy and hand-drawn cluster outlines remain outside these structural styles. Clone trees use supplied rooted topology; they do not reconstruct BCR lineages. The raincloud layout is an adaptation of violin/box/sample-dot conventions, not a claim of an identical source panel.

Structural styles and panel references 

layouts <- sn_list_plot_styles()
layouts <- layouts[layouts$kind == "structure" & !duplicated(layouts$style), ]
knitr::kable(layouts[c("function_name", "style", "reference", "data_requirements")])
function_name style reference data_requirements
sn_plot_matrix upper_triangle B 2024 Fig. 4L (single half adaptation) square matrix; identical ordered axis IDs
sn_plot_matrix lower_triangle B 2024 Fig. 4L (single half adaptation) square matrix; identical ordered axis IDs
sn_plot_matrix split_triangle B 2024 Fig. 4L x and compare; same axes and statistic
sn_plot_matrix circular CM Nature 2025 Fig. 4C named numeric matrix
sn_plot_matrix annotated CM Nature 2025 Fig. 2C and 4I row_annotation and/or column_annotation
sn_plot_matrix dendrogram NK 2023 Fig. 3A-B; B 2024 Fig. 4A finite matrix; Euclidean complete-linkage clustering
sn_plot_matrix grouped_bubble Fibroblast 2024 Fig. 1F and 3A/D independent color matrix x and area matrix size; named splits
sn_plot_matrix heatmap_bar CM Nature 2025 Fig. 5F named row_summary; statistic explicitly supplied
sn_plot_matrix heatmap_density Myeloid 2021 Fig. 4B; CM Nature 2025 Fig. 4D named column_summary; no automatic density inference
sn_plot_distribution violin_box NK 2023 Fig. 3G; T 2021 Fig. 2F numeric observations and groups
sn_plot_distribution raincloud adaptation of atlas violin/box/sample-dot grammar at least two observations per feature and group
sn_plot_distribution paired_box Myeloid 2021 Fig. 3E and 6C pair_by; one complete subject/group/feature observation
sn_plot_distribution paired_slope Fibroblast 2024 Fig. 6F; CM Nature 2025 Fig. 3G pair_by; optional sample_by aggregation
sn_plot_distribution split_violin CM Nature 2025 Fig. 4E exactly two groups; each feature is a row
sn_plot_distribution stacked_violin Myeloid 2021 Fig. 5C; Fibroblast 2024 Fig. 1D multiple features and groups
sn_plot_effect forest B 2024 Fig. 5A-C; T 2021 Fig. 4B and 5B label estimate lower upper; identity or positive ratio scale
sn_plot_effect diverging_bar B 2024 Fig. 3A; CM Nature 2025 Fig. 5J label and estimate; identity scale
sn_plot_effect lollipop NK 2023 Fig. 2A label and estimate; identity or ratio scale
sn_plot_overlap upset B 2024 Fig. 2C named sets of unique sample IDs
sn_plot_network bipartite Fibroblast 2024 Fig. 3I group_by defines exactly two partitions; cross-partition edges
sn_plot_network clone_tree B 2024 Fig. 3D supplied rooted topology; optional branch_length
sn_plot_network chord Fibroblast 2024 Fig. 6B non-negative weights; no directed arrows
sn_plot_network rewiring CM Nature 2025 Fig. 5I edges and compare_edges; common node table

Use sn_list_plot_styles("sn_plot_distribution") to discover styles accepted by one function. These styles are function-specific: style="upset" belongs to sn_plot_overlap(), not to an embedding renderer. The original sn_plot_heatmap(mode="average") accepts matrix structures and forwards annotation/summary arguments through ...; sn_plot_violin() also accepts violin_box, raincloud, split_violin, and stacked_violin. Use sn_plot_distribution() for tables, explicit assay/layer choices and sample aggregation. Existing defaults remain unchanged.

The examples below are synthetic layout demonstrations. They are not the paper’s cancer data. The separate Nature workbook recipe uses original values.

set.seed(102)
m <- matrix(rnorm(24), 4, dimnames = list(paste0("State ", 1:4), paste0("Site ", 1:6)))
correlation <- cor(t(m))
p1 <- sn_plot_matrix(correlation, style = "split_triangle",
  compare = correlation * 0.6, midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1))
p2 <- sn_plot_matrix(m, style = "circular", midpoint = 0)
patchwork::wrap_plots(p1, p2)

split_triangle keeps x above and compare below the omitted diagonal. Both axes must have identical ordered IDs. Independent clustering is rejected. dendrogram clusters both axes using Euclidean distance and complete linkage; its new dendrogram is not claimed to match an unpublished paper tree.

annotation <- data.frame(system = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 3), row.names = colnames(m))
sn_plot_matrix(m, style = "annotated", column_annotation = annotation, midpoint = 0)

For heatmap_bar, supply row_summary = setNames(values, rownames(m)); for heatmap_density, supply column_summary = setNames(values, colnames(m)). These tracks display your supplied statistic. grouped_bubble requires an independent non-negative size matrix plus a named row_split or column_split; area zero remains invisible.

samples <- data.frame(subject = rep(paste0("P", 1:12), 2),
  condition = rep(c("Pre", "Post"), each = 12),
  score = c(rnorm(12), rnorm(12, 1)))
a <- sn_plot_distribution(samples, "score", "condition", style = "raincloud")
b <- sn_plot_distribution(samples, "score", "condition", style = "paired_box", pair_by = "subject")
patchwork::wrap_plots(a, b)

Paired plots require one observation per subject/group/feature and complete pairs across groups. For cell-level tables, aggregate using a unique specimen sample_by column and identify matched patients with pair_by. The plot does not pair by row order, impute missing subjects or calculate a P value. split_violin draws two horizontal half densities per feature, each normalized to its own maximum width, with median marks; width is not relative cell count.

effects <- data.frame(label = c("NK", "B", "Myeloid"),
  estimate = c(-0.5, 0.2, 0.8), lower = c(-0.8, -0.1, 0.4), upper = c(-0.2, 0.5, 1.2))
a <- sn_plot_effect(effects, style = "forest", value_label = "Coefficient (95% CI)")
b <- sn_plot_overlap(list(B = c("S1", "S2", "S3"), T = c("S2", "S4"), Myeloid = c("S2", "S3")))
patchwork::wrap_plots(a, b)

For HR/OR forests use scale="ratio" and strictly positive supplied intervals; the reference becomes one and the axis logarithmic. identity uses zero. UpSet bars count exclusive intersections; every ID belongs to exactly one bar. Empty intersections are omitted; duplicate IDs within a set are rejected.

links <- data.frame(source = c("A", "A", "B"), target = c("B", "C", "D"), weight = c(1, 3, 2))
a <- sn_plot_network(links, style = "clone_tree")
b <- sn_plot_network(links, style = "chord", weight_label = "Supplied interaction weight")
patchwork::wrap_plots(a, b)

clone_tree requires a connected rooted tree; its default branch distance is unit edge depth, or the supplied branch_length column. chord requires non-negative weights; ribbon endpoints and sector widths encode incident weight, not node counts. bipartite uses two explicit node groups. rewiring accepts compare_edges; both panels share node coordinates and edge scales, retaining absent edges as absent. None infer biological interactions.

The repository’s scripts/smoke/atlas-figure-layouts.R exports all 23 styles to PDF/PNG and source-data bundles, with an independent 408-value Nature readback.

Compare the reusable styles 

sn_list_plot_styles()
#> # A tibble: 40 × 7
#>    style          description     reference changes_analysis kind  function_name
#>    <chr>          <chr>           <chr>     <lgl>            <chr> <chr>        
#>  1 classic        Original funct… NA        FALSE            theme ggplot rende…
#>  2 atlas          Compact atlas … NK Cell … FALSE            theme ggplot rende…
#>  3 atlas_outline  Outlined bubbl… Myeloid … FALSE            theme ggplot rende…
#>  4 atlas_module   Module-oriente… Cellular… FALSE            theme ggplot rende…
#>  5 upper_triangle upper triangul… B 2024 F… FALSE            stru… sn_plot_matr…
#>  6 lower_triangle lower triangul… B 2024 F… FALSE            stru… sn_plot_matr…
#>  7 split_triangle two matrices i… B 2024 F… FALSE            stru… sn_plot_matr…
#>  8 circular       annular heatma… CM Natur… FALSE            stru… sn_plot_matr…
#>  9 annotated      heatmap with c… CM Natur… FALSE            stru… sn_plot_matr…
#> 10 dendrogram     heatmap with r… NK 2023 … FALSE            stru… sn_plot_matr…
#> # ℹ 30 more rows
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: data_requirements <chr>

atlas uses solid marks and clean atlas panels; atlas_outline uses thin outlined bubbles and open boxplots; atlas_module uses sequential purple activity maps and grey network edges. These are shared presets, not claims that every panel in one paper has the same palette. Signed matrices can use midpoint = 0; Ro/e matrices can use midpoint = 1. Supply limits explicitly when comparing panels on a common scale. No automatic log transform or significance conversion occurs.

The following is the real 80-cell pbmc_small teaching dataset distributed with SeuratObject, with its original identities and t-SNE. It is not data from the six cancer papers and is not a validation of their cell labels.

pbmc <- SeuratObject::pbmc_small
sn_plot_dim(pbmc, reduction = "tsne", style = "atlas", raster = FALSE)

markers <- list(B = c("MS4A1", "CD79A"), T = c("CD3D", "CD2"))
plots <- lapply(c("classic", "atlas", "atlas_outline"), function(style) {
  sn_plot_dot(pbmc, features = markers, style = style) + ggplot2::ggtitle(style)
})
patchwork::wrap_plots(plots, nrow = 1)

sn_plot_heatmap(pbmc, unlist(markers), layer = "data", mode = "average",
                style = "atlas_outline")

Atlas dot styles currently reject split_by: Seurat’s split-dot color encoding differs from a shared quantitative scale. Use named feature blocks or separate panels with explicitly matched limits. Heatmap atlas styles currently require backend = "ggplot2"; the other heatmap renderers retain their native controls.

Reproduce Nature Fig. 2c from its source numbers

The publisher provides a source workbook for Fig. 2. Sheet Fig. 2c, after its first explanatory row, contains 12 CMs and 34 tissue columns. Some very small numbers are stored as scientific-notation text; as.numeric() parses them without adding pseudocounts. The recipe below preserves all 408 values and their source order. Color is capped at 3 for display while source values remain intact. The paper’s dendrogram and exact color lookup are not reconstructed; this is a new rendering of the supplied numerical matrix, not a modified copy of the original figure. The original figures are not bundled with Shennong.

d <- readxl::read_excel("41586_2025_9053_MOESM6_ESM.xlsx",
                         sheet = "Fig. 2c", skip = 1)
roe <- vapply(d[-1], as.numeric, numeric(nrow(d)))
rownames(roe) <- d[[1]]
p <- sn_plot_matrix(roe, style = "atlas_module",
                     palette = c("#FFFFFF", "#FCAE91", "#CB181D"), limits = c(0, 3),
                     value_label = "Ro/e", title = "CM tissue prevalence")
stopifnot(identical(attr(p, "shennong_figure_data")$matrix, roe))
sn_export_figure_bundle(p, "cm-fig2c", width = 240, height = 115)

Read-only numeric source matrices are retained in the plot’s shennong_figure_data attribute. Figure bundles write them as CSV with an explicit .shennong_row column (or a collision-free variant), together with the PDF/PNG, figure specification and checksummed manifest. Network bundles include separate original edge/node tables and rendered coordinates.

The repository script scripts/smoke/atlas-figure-styles.R downloads this workbook only when invoked with --download, records its URL and SHA-256, exports the figure, reads the CSV back and verifies every value. It also produces a PDF/PNG comparison gallery. Running it without --download uses the existing local workbook and fails clearly if it is missing.

Supplied matrix and network examples

The next examples use explicitly artificial numbers to demonstrate the interface; they are not reported biological findings.

score <- matrix(c(0.4, 1.2, 1.8, 0.7, 1, NA), 2,
                dimnames = list(c("State A", "State B"), c("Site 1", "Site 2", "Site 3")))
frequency <- score; frequency[] <- c(5, 20, 40, 10, 15, 0)
sn_plot_matrix(score, type = "bubble", size = frequency,
                midpoint = 1, style = "atlas_outline",
                value_label = "Ro/e", size_label = "Frequency (%)",
                title = "Artificial interface example")

edges <- data.frame(source = c("A", "A", "B", "C"),
                    target = c("B", "C", "D", "D"),
                    weight = c(0.3, 0.8, 0.4, 0.6))
nodes <- data.frame(node = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "Isolate"),
                    lineage = c("Group 1", "Group 2", "Group 1", "Group 3", "Group 2"))
sn_plot_network(edges, nodes, group_by = "lineage", style = "atlas_module",
                 weight_label = "Supplied score",
                 title = "Artificial topology; no CM inference")

Main-figure inventory

This index classifies 38 main figures. Routes identify useful renderers; they do not promise every listed subpanel is reproduced by one function. Existing trajectory/velocity views retain their own presentation controls. The three CSV catalogs (papers, figures and layouts) are installed under system.file("extdata", package = "Shennong"), so the classifications and verification status remain inspectable.

inventory <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "zhang-atlas-figures.csv",
                                package = "Shennong"))
for (paper in papers$paper) {
  cat("\n\n### ", paper, "\n\n", sep = "")
  rows <- inventory[inventory$paper == paper, -1]
  print(knitr::kable(rows))
}
